options: A command-line runner for Postman collections
questions.explanation: Newman runs exported (or API-fetched) collections from a terminal, which makes them usable in CI.

questions.prompt: Which option passes an environment file to Newman?
questions.explanation: `-e`/`--environment` loads an environment file. `--env-var` sets single variables, `-g` loads globals, `--folder` selects a folder.

questions.prompt: `newman run` exits with a non-zero code when an assertion fails, which lets CI fail the build.
questions.explanation: A non-zero exit code is how the pipeline knows the run failed. That is why Newman suits CI.

questions.prompt: Which command sets a secret from a CI variable without writing it into the environment file?
options: export apiKey and Newman reads it automatically
questions.explanation: `--env-var name=value` overrides an environment variable for the run. Newman does not read shell variables automatically, and there is no `--apiKey` option.

questions.prompt: You want to run the same collection once per row of a CSV file. Which option do you use?
questions.explanation: `-d`/`--iteration-data` runs one iteration per row with columns as variables. `-r` selects reporters and `-n` sets the number of iterations.

questions.prompt: Which reporters are commonly used in CI with Newman? Select all that apply.
options: junit for test results the CI server can display
htmlextra (a separate npm package) for a readable HTML report
questions.explanation: cli and junit are built in; htmlextra is a widely used external reporter installed separately. There is no jmeter reporter.

questions.prompt: Your CI job runs `newman run ... || true` so the HTML report is always published. Months later you discover failing tests never failed the build. What is the better approach?
options: Remove `|| true`; publish the report in a step configured to run even on failure (e.g. `if: always()`)
Keep `|| true` and read the report manually
questions.explanation: `|| true` swallows the exit code. CI systems can run publishing steps after a failure, so you keep both the report and a red build.

questions.prompt: A collection passes locally but every request fails in CI with ECONNREFUSED to localhost:8080. What is the most likely cause?
options: The CI run uses an environment whose baseUrl points to localhost, where no API is running in the CI container
questions.explanation: ECONNREFUSED means nothing is listening at that address. The environment used in CI must point to the deployed test API (or the job must start the API first).

coding.title: Summarise a JUnit report
coding.prompt: Newman's junit reporter writes XML like `<testsuites><testsuite name="Login"><testcase name="status is 200"/><testcase name="has token"><failure message="expected undefined"/></testcase></testsuite></testsuites>`. Write `summarise(xml_text)` returning `{'total': n, 'failed': n, 'failures': ['<suite> / <case>', ...]}` in document order. A testcase with a `<failure>` or `<error>` child counts as failed.
coding.starter:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

def summarise(xml_text):

coding.explanation: JUnit XML is the lingua franca of CI test results. Parsing it lets you post a short summary to chat or fail a job on specific suites. Note `is not None`: an Element with no children is falsy, so `if case.find('failure')` would be wrong.
hints: Compare `find(...)` with `is not None`, not truthiness.

tests.name: Counts and lists failures
tests.code:
x = '<testsuites><testsuite name="Login"><testcase name="status is 200"/><testcase name="has token"><failure message="m"/></testcase></testsuite></testsuites>'
assert summarise(x) == {'total': 2, 'failed': 1, 'failures': ['Login / has token']}, summarise(x)

tests.name: Errors count as failures
tests.code:
x = '<testsuites><testsuite name="A"><testcase name="a1"><error/></testcase></testsuite><testsuite name="B"><testcase name="b1"/></testsuite></testsuites>'
assert summarise(x) == {'total': 2, 'failed': 1, 'failures': ['A / a1']}
